requirements.name: prompt override options discovered from custom harness prompts
key UX: The backend discovers available prompt overrides from markdown files under custom-harness/prompts-override during server startup.
Each prompt file name becomes a stable option value, so selecting normal resolves to custom-harness/prompts-override/normal.md.
Only top-level markdown prompt files are exposed to the client as selectable prompt override options.
The discovered prompt override list is treated as startup-time configuration and does not change until the server restarts.

requirements.name: session bootstrap exposes prompt override options and selected value
key UX: The session bootstrap payload includes options.promptOverrides so the settings UI reflects the actual prompt files available in Custom Harness.
The active thread session metadata includes the currently applied prompt override value when one is in effect.
A cleared prompt override is represented explicitly so the client does not fall back to a stale selection.

requirements.name: runtime settings provide prompt override selection with safe fallback behavior
key UX: The settings drawer exposes a Prompt override select with a built-in None option.
The selected override is stored as runtimeSettings.promptOverride and sent with chat requests as thread-scoped runtime state.
If a previously selected override is no longer available, the UI preserves it as an unavailable value instead of silently dropping it.

requirements.name: prompt override resolves to base instructions on thread start
key UX: When a new thread starts with a selected prompt override, the backend reads the matching prompt file content.
The resolved prompt content is forwarded to Codex as thread baseInstructions during thread/start.
If no override is selected, the thread starts without injected baseInstructions and uses the default harness behavior.
An empty prompt file is valid and is forwarded as an explicit blank baseInstructions override.

requirements.name: prompt override reapplies through thread resume when the selection changes
key UX: Continuing an existing thread compares the requested prompt override with the override already applied to the thread.
When the selected override changes or is cleared, the backend resumes the thread with the correct baseInstructions before starting the next turn.
When the selected override is unchanged, the backend avoids unnecessary resume work and continues the thread directly.
Prompt override resolution during resume uses the startup-time prompt snapshot instead of re-reading modified files from disk.

requirements.name: prompt override resolution fails clearly for missing or invalid prompt files
key UX: Selecting a prompt override whose file cannot be found produces a direct backend error instead of silently falling back to default behavior.
Unreadable or invalid prompt files fail the request with a resolver error that makes the problem visible during send or resume.
Error handling stays scoped to prompt resolution and does not corrupt the stored thread metadata.

requirements.name: prompt override metadata remains authoritative across bootstrap and tab takeover
key UX: When a thread is resumed in another tab, the applied prompt override remains authoritative over stale local preferences.
The resumed thread metadata tells the client which prompt override is currently active on that thread.
Explicitly clearing the override persists as authoritative thread state until the user selects a new override.
